a894be235a0f82062b5215e6a4aa1f04d8a5ab89.summary: Check Point Research reports on Scattered Spider, a social-engineering group active since at least 2022 that is now also targeting aviation alongside enterprises. Media reports and advisories are cited as linking the group to airline attacks, including a July 2025 Qantas breach. Check Point identified about 500 phishing domains that follow the group's naming patterns, some aimed at technology, retail, aviation and other sectors, though not all are confirmed malicious. Noted tools include remote access utilities, Mimikatz, several infostealers and the BlackCat/ALPHV ransomware service.…

a801794d4e3d424e5e336407406ad9bfb975d934.summary: Report on a cybersecurity incident at Henry Schein, Inc., disclosed October 15. The company took systems offline, disrupting some operations. The report says AlphV (BlackCat) claimed responsibility and re-encrypted systems after negotiations broke down. By November 26 the company expected its US ecommerce platform to be restored within days. The report says customer bank accounts and card numbers may have been affected, and supplier bank account information was misused.

a8fc4a0fc73d95fe3761368fc6409cb730725369.summary: Radware report on the 8220 Gang, a for-profit group the report describes as from China and active since 2017. It mainly targets cloud providers and poorly secured applications with a custom crypto miner and IRC bot. It spreads via public exploits, brute-force attacks, Pastebin, Git and malicious Docker images. Cited cases include CVE-2022-26134 in Atlassian Confluence and a botnet of over 30,000 hosts. The report also covers Redis exploitation, including the Redigo backdoor.

a8b545dfb59cd2f81cdbd75dda219aafd80b1a99.summary: Morphisec Labs analysis of the JSSLoader, a .NET remote access trojan used by FIN7 (Carbanak Group). The report describes an attack chain it says was intercepted in a customer network in December 2020: a phishing invoice lure, VBScript stages run in memory, a scheduled task with a timeout delay, and a Takeout script that reflectively loads Carbanak. It notes links to QBOT, Egregor and BlackTDS, and says the C2 hosting provider is FranTech Solutions, previously used by FIN7.

a8edf171df1c5a7c53a0812f9f2391c3dbfa890a.summary: The report, from BleepingComputer, says the North Korean state-sponsored group Kimsuky reportedly suffered a data breach. Two hackers, 'Saber' and 'cyb0rg', leaked an 8.9GB dump of its backend, published with Phrack #72 at DEF CON 33. The dump reportedly exposes phishing kits and phishing tooling, Cobalt Strike loaders, reverse shells, and data touching South Korean government and Taiwan government and military sites. The outlet had not yet confirmed the leaked documents with researchers.

a8621f55d0056c799196bb6df4ba0273555b3d17.summary: Blog article (17 February 2021) by Avigayil Mechtinger of Intezer, part 3 of an ELF Linux malware series on dynamic analysis: processes, system calls, persistence, network sniffing and sandboxes. It walks through a stripped, statically linked sample that Intezer Analyze classifies as Reekoobe, based on code reused from earlier Rekoobe samples. The sample creates a service named likemae, copies itself to /usr/bin/likemae, and repeatedly tries to reach a command-and-control host that refuses the connection, a dead end for the analysis. It gains persistence only when run as a privileged user.
